messages:
Camille: Quick design review — noticed the model catalog rows feel visually equal but some rows are actually 'pinned' or 'priority'. Can we surface that state more clearly?
Amar: Agree. Right now the only hint is the tiny pin icon. Hard to scan.
Liam: Could be useful to have a left-edge accent or a subtle row background for priority rows. 1px border + 8% tint maybe.
Jen: Concern: contrast/a11y. Any accent must pass AA for text and focus outlines.
Camille: Good call. Maybe use an outline that appears only on hover/focus, but an always-visible badge for discovery.
Samira: What about adding a small labeled chip at the start: "PRIORITY" (uppercase) — that helps keyboard users and screen readers if we add aria-labels.
Amar: I sketched a couple options: (A) chip + subtle left stripe, (B) full-row subtle shade, (C) icon + accessible label. Prefer A because it's compact.
Camille: Can you paste the quick sketch?
Amar: ```
[ ] | PRIORITY | Model name  | perf badges | tags
[ ] |          | Model name  | perf badges | tags
```
Liam: I like that. Also thinking about filters discovery — when a user toggles the "priority" filter, the filter pill should stick to the top of the compare rail and include count.
Jen: Copy nit: "priority" might be ambiguous. Maybe call it "Pinned / Priority" or let users rename pins in settings.
Samira: Accessibility: screen readers should see the chip as a role="status" or live region when toggled? That might be noisy. Instead add aria-describedby on the row linking to a hidden label "Pinned for release X".
Camille: Good detail. For keyboard focus, tab into the row should land on the chip first. Chip should be actionable (unpin).
Amar: On performance badges: the red/yellow/green semantics are overloaded. Some models with slightly lower throughput show yellow; engineers asked to show numeric median latency on hover.
Liam: Hover card with median P95 + tokens/sec and a link to the per-model perf page sounds ideal. Keep the badge color to indicate pass/warn/fail relative to SLA.
Samira: Make sure hover cards are reachable via keyboard (focus on badge opens same card).
Jen: Copy for hover: "Latency: 85ms (P50), 210ms (P95) — Throughput: 120 tok/s" — short and scannable.
Camille: Also a UX question: when user pins a model inside compare, should that pin propagate to the catalog (global pin) or be local to the compare session? We had mixed feedback.
Amar: Propose local-by-default, with a small "Make global" toggle on the confirmation toast. Avoid surprising global changes.
Liam: Totally. Global pins should require explicit action.
Samira: Accessibility implication: when a pin is made global, fire an announcement: "Model X pinned globally".
Camille: Small alignment nit: current badge cluster pushes action menu off-screen at narrow widths. Can we reorder so actions are last and always visible?
Amar: Reorder: [selection checkbox] [priority chip] [name + version] [perf badges] [tags] [actions]. That should keep actions stable.
Jen: Test on 768px width and with long model names. Also test with screen reader and keyboard nav.
Camille: OK next steps: Amar to update mockups for chip + stripe variant and add keyboard flows; Liam to draft hover card content; Samira to write ARIA recommendations; Jen to sanity-check copy and contrast. I'll consolidate into one figma frame.
Amar: Working on it — will drop in #design-assets today. :sparkles:
DesignBot: Reminder — file checklist: accessibility notes, keyboard flows, copy strings, and responsive breakpoints.
Camille: Thanks — let's review again after mocks land. :thumbsup:
